cost: Admission O(key or heap-name bytes) before lookup or lazy load; hashing O(key bytes), expected O(1) probes. Heap O(H), load/save O(bytes), loaded caches retained. No performance claim.
description: Heap/local u64 IDs and append-oriented lazy registry with checked heap exhaustion and framing-safe key and heap-name admission.
forward: Id(h,l)=(u64(h)<<32)|l. open creates keys/ and reads heap triples. heap rejects names containing LF or ending in CR, then resolves existing name/kind or checked(max same-kind+1), checking range before push. id rejects tab/LF/CR before lazy I/O, lookup or mutation; admitted keys reuse or append exact bytes. keys_of loads consecutive indices1..; save appends unsaved suffixes. find/key and open retain legacy decoding.
inverse: Id uniquely splits to(heap,local); key reconstruction needs registry. key missing/out-of-range/zero returns empty string ambiguously. Saved table admits different caches/saved counters, not full state reconstruction.
Legacy trailing-CR decode can merge original key histories; this admission fix does not reconstruct or migrate historical keys. find/key retain prior decode behavior.
Legacy CRLF heap rows decode to the CR-free name and LF-split rows fail open or add triples; heap admission prevents new cases but does not repair or reinterpret old files.
limitations: No concurrent/crash/flush-fault/huge key-count tests. Old release wrapping is source-derived; old debug witness retained.
Partial lexical AST; no semantic proof or useful executable percentage surrogate.

Invalid-key errors precede lazy I/O and legacy cached lookup; invalid heap-name errors precede kind conflict and exhaustion. Old ambiguous CR keys and heap rows, duplicate imported heap names or numbers, failed buffered flushes and crash/concurrent recovery remain outside the roundtrip claims.
state: Rejected keys preserve cache/maps/names/counters/heaps; rejected heap names preserve heaps and saved_heaps with no I/O. Stable admitted-key IDs require consecutive unique keys, well-formed unique heap metadata with admitted names, one writer, representable indices and successful actual I/O. local0 stays reserved; checked heap exhaustion preserves heap state.
